issues.legal_issue: A lump-sum payment made toward construction costs, in addition to separately stipulated rent, is not advance rent without contractual terms or other cogent evidence establishing that character.
material_facts: The lease separately stipulated monthly rent and described the lump sum as a contribution toward the cost of constructing the cinema house.
The lease did not provide for the lump sum to be adjusted against rent or repaid.
The lessees required the building to be completed for use as a cinema, and the lessor lacked sufficient funds to complete it to their requirements.
The authorities inferred that the lump sum was advance rent, but there was no cogent evidence that the agreed monthly rent understated the property's rental value.
issues.conclusion: The lump sum could not be treated as advance rent on the lease terms and evidence in the case.
issues.legal_principle: The character of a payment must be determined from the terms of the transaction and the supporting evidence; a separately stipulated rent does not make a construction-cost contribution advance rent absent a contractual basis or cogent evidence for that inference. Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act distinguishes premium, a single payment, from rent, recurring payments during the lessee's enjoyment. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa v. Visweshwar Singh and Henriksen v. Grafton Hotel Ltd.

rule.if: income_tax_receipt_classification_case and rent_terms_separately_fixed and lump_sum_without_rent_adjustment and no_cogent_evidence_of_higher_rent

predicates.income_tax_receipt_classification_case: A court is deciding the character of a receipt for income-tax purposes.
predicates.rent_terms_separately_fixed: The parties stipulated rent separately from the disputed payment.
predicates.lump_sum_without_rent_adjustment: The payer made a lump-sum payment with no term requiring it to be credited against rent or repaid.
predicates.no_cogent_evidence_of_higher_rent: The tax authorities did not produce cogent evidence that the stipulated rent understated the property's rental value.

issues.definition: When an income-tax receipt dispute involves separately fixed rent, a lump sum unconnected by the agreement to rent, and no cogent proof that the rent was understated, the lump sum is not advance rent.

issues.legal_issue: A non-recurring lump-sum premium paid in connection with a lease is a capital receipt rather than a revenue receipt where the circumstances do not establish that it represents rent.
material_facts: The lessees paid a one-time lump sum toward construction of the premises, without a provision to adjust it against rent or repay it.
The lease separately fixed monthly rent, which was to begin after the lease was made.
The lessees took possession after construction was complete.
The tax authorities did not establish facts showing that the payment was revenue in character or that the stipulated rent was unreasonably low.
issues.conclusion: The lump sum had the characteristics of a capital payment and was not a revenue receipt.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a premium or salami is capital or revenue depends on the facts and circumstances of the case. Prima facie, premium or salami is not income, and the income-tax authorities must show facts that make it a revenue receipt. Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act distinguishes a single premium from recurring rent. The Court applied the principles in Member for the Board of Agricultural Income-tax v. Sindhurani Chaudhurani, and relied on Henriksen v. Grafton Hotel Ltd. and Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa v. Visweshwar Singh, which discussed Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal v. Shaw Wallace & Company.

rule.if: income_tax_receipt_classification_case and lump_sum_nonrecurring and rent_stipulated_separately and rent_begins_after_lease_grant and possession_follows_completion and not tax_authorities_proved_revenue_character

predicates.income_tax_receipt_classification_case: A court is deciding the character of a receipt for income-tax purposes.
predicates.lump_sum_nonrecurring: The payer made a single payment that was not recurring.
predicates.rent_stipulated_separately: The parties fixed rent separately from the disputed payment.
predicates.rent_begins_after_lease_grant: The agreed rent was payable from a time after the lease was granted.
predicates.possession_follows_completion: The lessee took possession after the leased premises had been completed.
predicates.tax_authorities_proved_revenue_character: The tax authorities established facts showing that the payment was revenue in character.

issues.definition: When an income-tax receipt dispute concerns a non-recurring lump sum separate from rent, with rent beginning after the lease and possession following completion, the payment is capital rather than revenue if the tax authorities do not prove its revenue character.
